meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'vegetarian' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вегетарианцы — это люди, которые не едят мясо.
examples.trans: Vegetarians are people who do not eat meat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Samsonov, I asked you not to!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from, out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beef').
Borrowed via German 'Pastete' from Old French/Italian 'pâté'/'pastetto', referring to finely ground seasoned meat or liver.

examples.trans: The chef prepares a signature pâté.
Chef, this is simply amazing pâté!

examples.text: Костя, быстро попробуй мой новый паштет.
examples.trans: Kostya, quickly taste my new pâté.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to carry to, take to', paired with 'относить'.

examples.text: Я сам отнесу блюдо в зал.
examples.trans: I will carry the dish into the dining room myself.
Take the documents to the boss.

examples.text: Я сейчас сам отнесу в зал.
examples.trans: I will carry it to the hall myself right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to eat', paired with 'съесть'.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
I'm at home because I'm ill.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, rubbish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Потому что я такой фигней заниматься не буду.
examples.trans: Because I am not going to bother with that nonsense.

заниматься.gloss: to be busy with, to do

meanings.en: to be busy with, to do
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ниматься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be busy with, to do', paired with 'заняться'.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'cutlet' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Но сочные мясные котлеты такие вкусные!
examples.trans: But juicy meat cutlets are so tasty!

examples.text: Вот мои вкусные котлеты для шефа.
examples.trans: Here are my tasty chops for the Chef.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cucumber' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И огурцы тоже можно, можно всё, что хотите! Получаются уникальные вкусы.
examples.trans: And cucumbers are fine too, anything you want! You get unique flavours.

examples.text: И огурцы тоже можно, можно всё, что хотите!
examples.trans: And cucumbers are fine too, anything you want!

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to prepare, to cook, to make
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to cook, to make', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common Russian noun meaning 'little roll' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мясные рулетики из телятины с тонкими ломтиками ветчины.
examples.trans: You know, veal rolls with thin slices of ham.
Maksim, will you make the rolls?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

уметь.gloss: to know how to, to be able to

meanings.en: to know how to, to be able to
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know how to, to be able to', paired with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'говаривать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'persuade'.

examples.text: Не уговаривай меня остаться здесь, в тепле.
examples.trans: Do not persuade me to stay here in the warmth.

examples.text: Да не буду я её уговаривать.
examples.trans: I am not going to persuade her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'all right, OK', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

пошутить.gloss: to joke, to make a joke

meanings.en: to joke, to make a joke
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'шутить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to joke, to make a joke', paired with 'шутить'.

examples.text: Я смотрю, вы легковерный! Я же пошутила!
examples.trans: I see you're gullible! I was only joking!
Don't be offended, I was only joking.

examples.text: Может быть, шеф просто неудачно пошутил?
examples.trans: Maybe the chef was just joking unsuccessfully?
